newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: BOK steps in to slow won's rise vs dlr - dealers.
newsitem.headline: BOK steps in to slow won's rise vs dlr - dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea intervened in the foreign exchange market in early Monday afternoon to slow the won's rise versus the dollar, dealers said.
The central bank, as it normally does, denied it intervened.
Dealers said the central bank stepped in after the won rose to a day high of 822.80. The won soon fell back to the 826 level.
"The central bank came in to tell the market that it doesn't want the dollar to fall too quickly," said one dealer.
Dealers said the local unit had been gaining recently on the back of export deals and bullish sentiment.
At 0544 GMT, The won is currently trading at 826.70, compared with a six-year low of 834.50 on October 29.
